Answer: C
Reason: The initial images (Figures 4a and 4b) demonstrate a right lower lobe parenchymal opacity accompanied by blunting of the costophrenic angle, indicative of a pleural effusion. The follow-up image (Figure 5) shows resolution of the acute consolidation but reveals residual linear scarring and pleural thickening, an evolution characteristic of a healed pulmonary infarction.
